steps.text: Grease a 10x15 inch pan. In a large bowl, combine 1 1/2 cups melted margarine, peanut butter, confectioners' sugar and graham cracker crumbs. Spread in prepared pan.

Combine 1/2 cup margarine and chocolate chips in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir occasionally until melted and smooth. Spread over peanut butter mixture. Let cool completely before cutting into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Candy Bars
raw_recipe.description: No-bake bars with a peanut butter graham cracker base and a chocolate top.

review.reviewBody: YUM!! Although I mixed dark and semi-sweet chocolate with this recipe, I do not recommend it. BUT it was still the best peanut butter candy recipe I've ever made. The peanut butter mix (w/o the chocolate) tastes like "buckeyes" that one makes at Christmas time. GREAT!! Will make it again and again. To the comment from Lara29: make sure you are using powdered (not regular!)sugar (4 1/2 cups is one box) because the amount is just perfect. Wouldn't change a thing :)

I also halved the bottom and put it in a 9x9" pan. If I were to make the full recipe, I'd double the chocolate topping. I made half with semi-sweet chocolate, and half with a Cadbury Dream bar (my fiance prefers white chocolate). We both enjoyed them.

I used butter instead of margarine and crunchy peanut butter in the mixture. I also made my peanut butter bars a bit thinner than suggested. I spread the mixture into a Calphalon 12 x 17 inch pan and then set the pan in the freezer for about a half an hour or so. The mixture set nicely in the freezer! (Can be stored in the fridge to ensure the bars don't fall apart and get "mushy".) 
*The thinner the better in the pan! Don't forget to freeze after! Yummy!
 I also posted a pic of my peanut butter bars.

OH MY GOSH these are PERFECTTTTTTTTTT. However, of course, I changed a few tiny things! I halved the PB mixture recipe and spread it in a 13 x 9 pan. Then I used 1.5 cups of melted semi sweet chocolate chips and mixed in about 3 T. of peanut butter for my topping (omit butter). Adding the PB helps keep the chocolate from cracking when you cut them. I also liked the ratio of peanut butter to chocolate topping. I like mine about 50/50. Mmm. I had tried "Peanut Butter Bars I" before I tried this recipe, but that recipe was a little too dry/gritty for my liking. This one still has the yummy graham cracker taste but it is MUCH more moist. I am in love with these!!!!!!!!

I've tried several different peanut butter bar recipes over the years, and this is my favorite. It's so easy AND delicious! I followed the recommendation of the previous reviewers and sprinkled a little sea salt over the peanut butter mixture, refrigerated it a bit, and then added the chocolate topping. I chilled it again before letting it come fully to room temperature to cut it. It cut pretty well, but next time I'm going to line the pan with foil so I can lift it out to cut it. That will be easier yet!

Made this Peanut Butter Candy Bar recipe at Christmas time. My husband and daughter can't get enough of it. I used someone's suggestion to line the pan with foil and then after the candy is set, remove the foil and candy all at once from the pan, place on a flat surface and cut into squares using a pizza cutter. Works great and makes for easy cutting. Thanks for sharing this recipe, KARILK.
Delicious. I halved the recipe for the bottom, but used the full amount for the chocolate top. It came out just right for a 9 x 13 pan.

Great recipe, can also be used to make peanut butter balls! Only thing I did different was used 3 cups of confectioners sugar instead of 4.5 cups! I did try to melt the chocolate with the butter and it didn't work so I remade it without the butter in the chocolate and it worked out, maybe that was just me doing it wrong, I don't know :)

Yum! The graham cracker crumbs give it the slightly "gritty" texture you get in the commercial peanut butter cups. Make sure you crush them extra fine though, to powder if you can. Also make sure you cut these small--big pieces become too overwhelming!

I made this today however I switched it up to my own liking...let sugar used butter not as much...and in between the layers I put in some smashed pecans and then used white chocolate over the top.... So delicious!

I had the same problem with not having enough choc. mixture for the top. I used an 11 x 13 glass dish, and the peanut butter part was really thick! I just doubled the choc. mixture, and it was perfect! I used one cup marg. instead of one and a half, and real chocolate chips. (The other half cup went into the extra choc. mix anyway!) I took it to a family potluck, and everybody loved it! This is a five star recipe with these modifications!
Wow! So incredible! It keeps well for several days too! My daughter said it actually tasted better after a couple of days in the fridge.
I used Splenda instead of sugar to make these diabetic friendly. Cut amount of sweetener by half and just love them.

This is the easiest, yummiest way to extend your Christmas cookies or wow your guests with a beautiful treat. So quick and easy to make with amazing flavor. I make with dark chocolate instead of semi-sweet. This is the peanut butter fudge from your childhood.
Soon good

This recipe did not set up AT ALL! The peanut butter layer stayed gooey and was impossible to cut into bars. I had to use a spoon to scoop it out of the pan. I followed the recipe exactly, but maybe the order I stirred together the ingredients caused the consistancy issue?
These are so good. Very much like the cups!

First of all, I never buy margarine. I used butter (homemade butter when I have time to make some). I love this recipe but I am not a huge fan of the 2 cups of graham cracker crumbs in this recipe; the crumbs seem to overwhelm the taste and texture where there is less peanut butter taste. I have made it with 1 cup of crumbs and it still seemed too much. The next time I make this recipe, I will increase the peanut butter, decrease the butter and crumbs.

I am a huge fan of the peanut butter cups recipe on this same website, which can also be made into bars.
Easy to make but came out super sweet.
Great candy! But don't use butter instead of margerine. Dosn't work as well.
